Title / Summary: Broken Socket.IO polling and client connection crashes due to dead hardcoded backend URL
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Load original Game Hub frontend.
2. Open browser console.
3. Observe repeated red network errors to http://localhost:3000/socket.io/.
4. Multiplayer completely broken.
Expected Behavior: Client should cleanly handle multiplayer without requiring an unreachable local Node.js server.
Observed / Buggy Behavior: Repeated ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED, high CPU polling overhead, and broken multiplayer room creation.
Root Cause Analysis: Frontend had hardcoded dependency on a local Express/Socket.IO backend that does not exist in serverless Vercel deployments.
Fix Implemented / Code Modification: Engineered serverless WebRTC peer-to-peer architecture (webrtc.ts) with direct data channels, shareable room codes, and QR code signaling.
Retest Verification & Evidence: Verified in TC-RTC-001 to TC-RTC-005. Zero network errors in console; P2P room creation works serverlessly on Vercel.

Title / Summary: Uncaught ReferenceError on window.localStorage in private browsing or headless test runs
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Run Vitest in Node.js environment or open app in strict private browsing with storage blocked.\n2. Attempt to save high score or load favorites.
Expected Behavior: Storage operations should gracefully fall back without throwing unhandled exceptions.
Observed / Buggy Behavior: Uncaught ReferenceError: localStorage is not defined, causing entire React component tree to crash to white screen.
Root Cause Analysis: Direct unshielded calls to `window.localStorage` without existence checks or in-memory fallback.
Fix Implemented / Code Modification: Implemented StorageEngine v2 with safe environment detection and automatic internal `memoryStore: Map<string, string>` fallback.
Retest Verification & Evidence: Verified in TC-STO-002 and automated unit test storage.test.ts (5/5 tests passing in Node environment).

Title / Summary: Non-functional mockup game cards on homepage leading to empty routes or unhandled exceptions
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Click on featured games on legacy home page.\n2. Observe broken routes, placeholder buttons, and missing game logic.
Expected Behavior: Every displayed game card should lead to a fully implemented, playable game engine.
Observed / Buggy Behavior: Clicking resulted in 404 routes or static placeholders with no interactive gameplay.
Root Cause Analysis: Legacy repo contained demo cards with static images that were not wired to real game components.
Fix Implemented / Code Modification: Implemented 8 fully playable browser game engines (Snake, 2048, Tetris, Minesweeper, Breakout, Checkers, Tic-Tac-Toe, Memory Match) and wired unified GamePlay router.
Retest Verification & Evidence: Verified in TC-CAT-004 and TC-SNK-001 through TC-MEM-005. All 8 games fully playable with score tracking.

Title / Summary: Vitest test runner version incompatibility with Vite 5.4 causing npm test failure
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Run `npm install -D vitest` without version constraint on Vite 5.4 project.\n2. Observe npm ERESOLVE peer dependency error.
Expected Behavior: Vitest should install cleanly and execute unit tests matching Vite 5.4.
Observed / Buggy Behavior: npm install crashed with conflicting peer dependencies (vitest 5.x requested vite >= 6.4.0).
Root Cause Analysis: Attempting to install latest bleeding-edge Vitest 5 into a Vite 5.4 project without pinning compatible semver.
Retest Verification & Evidence: Verified via `npm test -- --run`. All 9 test suites and 37 tests pass with 100% success rate in 1.46s.

Title / Summary: Checkers engine turn-locking defect where king promotion did not switch turn to opponent
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Play Checkers until red piece reaches row 7.\n2. Piece is promoted to king.\n3. Observe that active player turn did not toggle to black.
Expected Behavior: King promotion should crown piece and immediately pass turn to opponent unless jump sequence is available.
Observed / Buggy Behavior: Turn remained locked on promoted player; opponent could not make moves.
Root Cause Analysis: applyMove logic in CheckersEngine had an early return on promotion without updating `nextTurn` flag.
Fix Implemented / Code Modification: Refactored CheckersEngine promotion block to properly compute valid next moves and pass turn to opponent.
Retest Verification & Evidence: Verified in Checkers.test.ts and TC-CHK-004. King promotion succeeds and turn passes correctly.

Title / Summary: Minesweeper instant defeat on first click if user selected initial randomized mine
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Launch Minesweeper.\n2. Click cell [0, 0]. In ~15% of games, cell was a mine, triggering instant Game Over on first click.
Expected Behavior: First click must always be guaranteed safe per modern Minesweeper standards.
Observed / Buggy Behavior: Immediate defeat on first click frustrated users.
Root Cause Analysis: Mines were generated upfront during board initialization before first user click.
Fix Implemented / Code Modification: Implemented deferred mine placement: board generates mines dynamically only after first click, guaranteeing clicked cell and its 8 neighbors are mine-free.
Retest Verification & Evidence: Verified in Minesweeper.test.ts and TC-MSW-001. First click 100% guaranteed safe across 100 automated iterations.

Title / Summary: Missing mobile touch D-Pad controls on Snake, Tetris, and 2048 preventing mobile playability
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Snake, Tetris, or 2048 on a mobile device or touch viewport (375x812).\n2. No on-screen controls available; game unplayable without physical keyboard.
Expected Behavior: Touch-enabled devices should display responsive on-screen D-Pad and control buttons.
Observed / Buggy Behavior: Games were completely unplayable on smartphones and tablets.
Fix Implemented / Code Modification: Created responsive TouchControls component with virtual D-Pad buttons (Up, Down, Left, Right, Action, Rotate) displayed conditionally on mobile/tablet viewports.
Retest Verification & Evidence: Verified in TC-SNK-005 and EVD-011. Mobile touch D-Pad controls verified on 375x812 viewport.

Title / Summary: TypeScript compile error: MatchData type missing from storage export
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Run `npm run build` with PlayerManager importing `MatchData` from storage.\n2. Observe TS2305: Module storage has no exported member 'MatchData'.
Expected Behavior: Type exports should align across all consumption modules.
Root Cause Analysis: `storage.ts` defined type `Match` but PlayerManager was importing legacy alias `MatchData`.
Fix Implemented / Code Modification: Added `export type MatchData = Match;` type alias to `storage.ts`.
Retest Verification & Evidence: Verified via `npm run build` (tsc && vite build). Zero TypeScript errors.

Title / Summary: Settings modal volume sliders lacked keyboard accessibility ARIA attributes
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Inspect volume slider inputs using screen reader or accessibility audit tool.
Expected Behavior: Inputs should provide aria-label, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, and aria-valuenow.
Observed / Buggy Behavior: Accessibility audit flagged sliders as unlabelled range inputs.
Root Cause Analysis: Missing explicit ARIA attributes on custom range slider elements.
Fix Implemented / Code Modification: Added comprehensive `aria-label='Master Volume'`, `aria-valuemin='0'`, `aria-valuemax='100'`, and `aria-valuenow` attributes to all settings sliders.
Retest Verification & Evidence: Verified in TC-A11Y-003 and EVD-004. ARIA attributes verified in DOM inspection.
